title: How to Use Conditional Formatting in Google Sheets
dek: Conditional formatting colors a cell automatically based on its value — to highlight, rank, or flag data. Select your cells, open Format > Conditional formatting, and set a rule. Here is how to use single-color rules, color scales, and custom formulas.

seo.metaDescription: Use conditional formatting in Google Sheets to color cells by value: single-color rules, color scales, and custom formulas. A clear step-by-step guide.

sources.label: Google Docs Editors Help — Use conditional formatting rules

richText: Conditional formatting makes Google Sheets color your cells automatically based on what they contain, turning a plain table into something you can scan in seconds. Use it to highlight values above a target, flag overdue dates, or spot duplicates — and the colors update themselves as the data changes.

items: Select the cells you want to format.
In the panel on the right, choose a condition under "Format cells if…".
Pick the fill color (or text style), then click Done.

body.richText: To highlight duplicates, use a custom formula: =COUNTIF(A:A, A1)>1. Every value that appears more than once gets colored, which makes repeats easy to find before you clean them up.

items: To change a rule: open Format > Conditional formatting, click the rule, and edit it.
To delete a rule: hover over it in the panel and click the trash icon.
Rules apply top to bottom — the first matching rule wins, so drag them to reorder if two overlap.

items.question: How do I highlight an entire row in Google Sheets?
items.answerRichText: Select the whole range, choose Format > Conditional formatting > Custom formula is, and lock the column with a dollar sign — for example =$C1="Overdue". Because the column is fixed, the full row is colored whenever the test is true.

items.question: Why is my conditional formatting not working in Google Sheets?
items.answerRichText: Usually the range is wrong, the custom formula is missing the dollar sign, or a higher rule is overriding it. Open the Conditional formatting panel to check the range, the formula, and the order of the rules.

items.question: Can I copy conditional formatting to other cells?
items.answerRichText: Yes. Copy a formatted cell, select the target cells, then use Edit > Paste special > Conditional formatting only. The rules copy across and adjust to the new cells.
